title: How a Spacecraft Nudged an Asteroid's Orbit
post_title: How a Spacecraft Nudged an Asteroid's Orbit | QuantaTale
post_description: How NASA's DART crashed into an asteroid moon to change its orbit, and what ESA's Hera will check, from NASA and ESA. Sources: National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/mission/dart/ and European Space Agency https://www.esa.int/articles/about-us/directorates/operations/space-safety/hera/hera-mission-overview #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: Could we ever push a dangerous asteroid off course? The first mission built to test deflecting an asteroid was NASA's DART. In this kinetic impact method, you crash into an asteroid to shift where it is heading. DART's target was Dimorphos, a small body that orbits the larger asteroid Didymos. Dimorphos's orbit changed measurably, the first time humans have shifted a body's orbit. Many uncertainties remain about exactly what the impact did. ESA's Hera spacecraft will survey the asteroids afterwards to make the technique well understood and repeatable.
